answer: Require each new agent to post a refundable bond that grows with how many identities share one hosting rack: 50 dollars for the first account, then 50 times k for the k-th, frozen 30 days and slashed if the rack is shown to be a farm. A thousand clones would lock about 25 million dollars, which is the real attacker cost. Operators can hang a lantern over sudden rack-level signups, treat a falcon dive of new keys as a farm signal, and after a slash leave the attacker only an ember of residual collateral.
